context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
Category theory: ordinary functor between arbitrary categories C and D without assuming smallness; object/arrow assignments preserve identities and compositions.

Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.

Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.

Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
Commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: residue field A/m of a commutative local ring (A,m), including the prime-localized κ(p)=R_p/pR_p and the scheme-point κ(s)=O_{S,s}/m_s.
query: residue field of a local ring

context: Commutative algebra: associative commutative ring R with a specified multiplicative identity 1_R; the prime-ideal formulation does not assume the ring is an integral domain.
Module theory: free left R-module over a unital ring with an R-basis, equivalently a direct sum R^{(I)} of copies of R, possibly infinite rank.

Module theory: quotient left R-module M/N by an R-submodule N, whose elements are additive cosets m+N with addition and R-scalar action induced by M. Includes ideal modules I/I², successive filtration quotient modules and regular-module quotients R/I; extra ring, graded, flatness, or field structure is not part of this quotient-module meaning.
Set theory: injectivity of an arbitrary map f:X→Y, meaning f(x)=f(y) implies x=y for all x,y in X; for structured maps this is the underlying-set condition.

Set theory: surjective function f:X→Y whose image is the entire stated codomain Y; for module homomorphisms this is the underlying-set surjectivity of the R-linear map, independent of linearity, free domain, or choice of basis.
Category theory: f:X→Y is an isomorphism iff there exists g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y; no underlying-set bijectivity is assumed.

Commutative algebra: scalar extension of a commutative unital k-algebra R along field extension K/k, yielding the unital K-algebra R⊗_k K with induced multiplication (r⊗a)(s⊗b)=rs⊗ab and K-scalar structure.
Order theory: supremum sup(A) of subset A⊆S, an upper bound no greater than every other upper bound when it exists.
Category theory: hom-collection Hom_C(X,Y) of arrows X→Y; a preadditive category requires these collections to be sets carrying abelian group structures, without requiring all objects to form a set.

Polynomial algebra: a nonzero univariate polynomial f(X)=a_nX^n+⋯+a_0 over a commutative unital coefficient ring is monic if its leading coefficient a_n equals the multiplicative identity 1, including degree zero unit polynomial 1.
Algebraic geometry: distinguished principal open D(f)={p∈Spec(R):f∉p} of a commutative ring's affine spectrum.

Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.

Commutative algebra: kernel ideal of a unital homomorphism φ:A→B of commutative rings, consisting of all a∈A mapped to 0_B; for a polynomial evaluation map it is the ideal of polynomial relations, and for a quotient-localization composite it is the inverse image of zero in the target ring.

Module theory: direct sum ⊕_{i∈I} M_i of left R-modules, the module of families (m_i) of finite support with componentwise addition and scalar multiplication, distinct from their unrestricted product.
query: direct sum ⊕_i M_i of a family of modules

context: Set theory: binary intersection A∩U of two sets, whose elements belong to both A and U; applied to ambient open sets and a subspace.
Set theory: relative complement A\B={x∈A:x∉B} for two sets A,B⊆X; in the sigma-algebra axiom A,B are members of Σ.
Commutative algebra: commutative unital algebra A over a specified base field k, with a chosen unital structure homomorphism k→A; A need not be a field, a domain or geometrically regular.
query: commutative unital algebra over a field

context: Commutative algebra: principal ideal generated by one element

Set theory: bijective mapping f:X→Y, a function that is both injective and surjective onto the specified codomain Y; equivalently a function admitting a two-sided inverse Y→X. In structured settings this refers only to the underlying-set map, not to automatic continuity, R-linearity, group structure, or naturality.

Field theory: subfield k(B) of an extension K/k generated by k together with a subset B⊆K, the intersection of all intermediate subfields containing k∪B; for algebraically independent B, it identifies with a rational-function field in the elements of B.
query: subfield k(B) generated by k and B

context: Set theory: power set of an arbitrary underlying set X, namely the collection of all subsets of X; variable names X and S are interchangeable.

Commutative algebra: square-zero ideal I of a commutative unital ring A, characterized by I²={0} (equivalently ab=0 for all a,b∈I). The square-zero property is strictly stronger than mere nilpotence of an unspecified positive exponent.
General topology: open neighborhood of a point x∈X, an open subset U of X containing x.

Commutative algebra: for unital ring homomorphism φ:R→S and prime q⊆S, contraction p=φ^{-1}(q)⊆R, a prime ideal by inverse-image stability under ring homomorphisms; when φ is an inclusion this becomes q∩R.
Elementary number theory: positive integer p greater than one whose positive divisors are exactly 1 and p; this is an integer prime, not a prime ideal of a ring.

Order theory: a maximal element m in a nonempty family F of subsets of an ambient set, ordered by inclusion, is one with no distinct member B∈F properly containing m. Maximal need not mean greatest, and for ideals the family F is any specified nonempty subcollection of the ideals of R.
query: maximal element of a collection under inclusion

context: Category theory: parallel morphisms f,g:X→Y in a category, with identical source and codomain, forming a parallel-pair diagram.
Commutative algebra: isomorphism of unital R-algebras preserving both ring operations and the specified structure maps from R; not merely an abstract ring or R-module isomorphism.
query: R-algebra isomorphism from the quotient to S

context: Commutative algebra: evaluation R-algebra homomorphism ev_(a_i):R[X_i : i∈I]→A into a commutative unital R-algebra A, sending each formal indeterminate X_i to a specified a_i∈A and fixing the coefficients through the structure map R→A; includes univariate evaluation f(a) and the canonical R[X_s:s∈S]→S sending X_s to s.
Probability theory: finite absolute expectation E|X_t|<∞ of the real random variable X_t for every real time t≥0 in a stochastic process.
Commutative algebra/algebraic geometry: locus V(I)={p∈Spec(R):I⊆p} of prime ideals containing an ideal I in a commutative ring; these provide Zariski closed subsets.
Topology: subset U⊆Spec(R) both Zariski-open and Zariski-closed, an instance of the generic clopen predicate, not the idempotent correspondence itself.
General topology: closed F⊆X exactly when X\F is open in the specified topology; this depends on the ambient X and is distinct from Zariski-closed subschemes.
query: closed subset of a topological space

context: Polynomial algebra over fields: a root (zero) α∈K of a univariate polynomial f∈F[x] in a field extension K/F means f(α)=0_K using coefficient inclusion F→K and polynomial evaluation; includes the residue class of x in K=F[x]/(f) for nonconstant f.
query: roots of a polynomial in a field

context: Category theory: ordinary (size-unrestricted) groupoid G, a category in which every morphism has a two-sided inverse; no requirement that the object collection be a set or that hom-categories be small. Distinct from an explicitly small groupoid.

Point-set topology: quotient (final) topology induced by a surjective continuous map q:X→Q, where U⊆Q is open exactly when q^{-1}(U) is open in X; includes canonical quotient-set maps and the map X→f(X) when equipped with final topology, independently of whether a larger codomain Y is surjected onto.
query: quotient topology on Y for f

context: Commutative algebra: subset S of a commutative unital ring R, containing 1_R and closed under multiplication, used as denominators in ring or module localization.

Commutative algebra: tensor product S⊗_R R′ of commutative unital R-algebras S and R′, with induced commutative unital R′-algebra multiplication (s⊗r′)(t⊗u′)=st⊗r′u′; the base-change algebra underlying Spec(S⊗_R R′).
2-category theory: natural transformation α:H⇒K between functors over C whose component arrows project to identities id_{p(x)} in C.
query: natural transformations lying over identity arrows

context: Field theory: subfield F of a field E is a subset F⊆E containing 0_E,1_E and closed under inherited field addition, additive inverses, multiplication and inverses of nonzero elements of F, with induced field operations.

General topology: a continuous map f:X→Y is a closed map if every closed F⊆X has closed image f(F)⊆Y; here it is the underlying continuous map of a scheme base change, without a Hausdorff or properness assumption.
query: sends closed subsets to closed subsets

context: Real analysis: sequence (a_n) of real coefficients indexed by nonnegative integers, a function ℕ_0→ℝ; no assumption of convergence.

Commutative algebra: lift of an R-algebra homomorphism f:S→A/I across a surjective R-algebra map q:A→A/I, namely an R-algebra homomorphism g:S→A satisfying q∘g=f. Here I is square-zero and formal unramifiedness only requires uniqueness, not existence.

Module theory: product of an arbitrary indexed family of R-modules (Q_j)_{j∈J}, consisting of all tuples (q_j)∈∏_jQ_j with coordinatewise addition and scalar action; unlike a direct sum, supports need not be finite.
query: arbitrary direct product ∏_j Q_j of R-modules

context: Category theory: cone from vertex L to a diagram F:I→C, a natural transformation constant_L⇒F with compatible arrows L→F(i); not necessarily a limit cone.
query: cone arrows L→F(i) compatible with all arrows of I

context: Map of local rings taking preimage of target maximal ideal to source maximal ideal, stronger than an arbitrary unital ring homomorphism.
Algebraic geometry: family of distinguished opens D(f_i) in Spec(R) with union equal to Spec(R); the f_i need not all be the same and the localizations are taken on these opens.
query: cover of Spec(R) by standard opens D(f_i)

context: Module theory: submodule generated by a subset S of a left R-module M, consisting of all finite R-linear combinations of elements of S; for a finite S={m_1,...,m_n} this is the finite R-linear span Σ_i R m_i, possibly all of M.
Sheaf theory: homomorphism of sheaves of unital rings O_Y→f_*O_X on Y, where (f_*O_X)(V)=O_X(f^{-1}(V)), for continuous f:X→Y.

Module theory over a commutative unital ring R: ideal action IM on an R-module M, the R-submodule generated by all finite sums of products i*m with i∈I and m∈M; this includes (I^n)M for ideal powers I^n, but differs from ideal multiplication I^n alone and from forming a quotient module M/I^nM.

Field and polynomial algebra: polynomial P∈F[T] splits over extension E/F if its image in E[T] is a product c∏_j(T−α_j) of linear factors, including multiplicities, with nonzero scalar c and roots α_j∈E.
query: factors completely into linear factors over E

context: Category theory: contravariant Hom operation α:T'→T sends a morphism h:T→X to h∘α:T'→X and respects compositions/identity.

Probability: equality of two real random variables outside a P-null exceptional set, here conditional expectation E[X_{n+1}|F_n] and X_n for each fixed n≥0. The almost-sure equality notion is reusable; the conditional-expectation martingale identity is source-specific.
Set theory: arbitrary indexed intersection ⋂_{F∈𝔽}F of subsets of X, here 𝔽 comprises the closed F containing A; identifying this intersection with cl_X(A) is the definition of closure.
query: intersection of all closed supersets of A

context: Affine geometry: finite affine combination ∑_{i=1}^k α_i x_i of vectors or points with real coefficients ∑α_i=1, without positivity required.
Category theory: natural transformation a:F⇒G of functors C^op→Sets, with components a_U:F(U)→G(U) commuting with every restriction map.
Measure theory: extended nonnegative real numbers [0,+∞], adjoining +∞ to the set of ordinary nonnegative real numbers with usual extended arithmetic/order conventions.
Integral domains: divisibility relation between ring elements
Module theory: an R-module admitting a finite or countably infinite set of generators under R-linear combinations; no projectivity, flatness, or finitely-generated-only condition.
Linear algebra: dimension dim_F(V) of a vector space V over field F, the cardinality of any F-basis of V; for finite-dimensional V this is a nonnegative finite integer.
Set theory: transitivity property of a binary relation R⊆S×S, namely (x,y),(y,z)∈R imply (x,z)∈R for all x,y,z∈S.
query: transitivity x~y and y~z imply x~z

context: Analysis/orthogonal polynomial systems: a positive discrete weight function x↦w_x from a set X of distinct real support points to strictly positive reals, either finite or countable.
Commutative algebra: idempotent ring element e∈R satisfying e²=e, in a commutative unital ring; e=0 and e=1 allowed.
Order theory: total or linear order on S, a partial order for which every pair x,y is comparable (x≤y or y≤x).
Category theory: composition of arrows with matching codomain and domain, so a,b:Y→W may follow f:X→Y.
Commutative algebra: the unit ideal (1)=R of a unital ring R, containing 1_R and hence every element; here R=k[X].
Measure-theoretic polynomial orthogonality of distinct degrees, with zero mixed integral ∫p_n(x)p_m(x)dμ(x) under a specified nonnegative measure.
General topology: neighborhood N of point x if there exists an open U with x∈U⊆N, without requiring N to be open.
query: neighborhood of a point in a topological space

context: Ring theory: specified two-sided multiplicative identity 1_R in an associative ring R, satisfying 1_Rr=r1_R=r for all r∈R, with no commutativity requirement.
Algebra and module theory: restriction of scalars along unital ring homomorphism φ:R→S, giving the codomain S an R-module structure via r·s=φ(r)s; changing φ may change the action.
query: R-module structure on S induced by R→S

context: Module theory: canonical R-linear map M⊗_R(∏_iQ_i)→∏_i(M⊗_R Q_i) induced by projection π_i:∏_iQ_i→Q_i; injectivity for all families defines Mittag-Leffler property.
Real affine geometry: finite sum ∑_{j=1}^m λ_j u_j with m≥1, λ_j>0 and ∑ λ_j=1; zero weights can be omitted.
query: finite convex combination with strictly positive coefficients

context: Category theory: zero morphism 0_{X,C} in an additive Hom-set of a preadditive category; here the composite p∘f equals this zero arrow.
query: zero morphism and equation p composed with f equals zero

context: Multivariable real analysis: quotient [f(a+tu)−f(a)]/t for nonzero scalar t→0 and fixed vector direction u, with domain defined near a.

Sheaf theory and algebraic geometry: ring O_X(U) of sections of a sheaf of commutative unital rings O_X over an open subset U of X, with pointwise ring operations and restriction homomorphisms for inclusions V⊆U; distinct from a stalk O_{X,x}.
Set theory: indexed Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}X_i, the collection of functions/tuples selecting one x_i∈X_i for every index i.
Homological algebra: ith homology H_i(C_•)=ker(d_i:C_i→C_{i−1})/im(d_{i+1}:C_{i+1}→C_i) of a chain complex of modules.
Measure theory: σ-algebra σ(𝒜) generated by an arbitrary family 𝒜⊆P(X), the least σ-algebra on X containing 𝒜; Borel case specializes to 𝒜=τ.
query: generated sigma-algebra from open family tau

context: General topology: arbitrary indexed open cover (V_i) of X, with union X and no finite-subcover requirement.
Algebraic geometry: subsheaf of ideals I of O_X locally generated by sections over neighborhoods of points.
query: locally section-generated sheaf of ideals I⊆O_X

context: Strict 2-category theory: invertible 2-cell α:f⇒g in the hom-category C(X,Y), admitting a vertical inverse β:g⇒f satisfying vertical identity composites.
Stochastic process theory: increasing σ-algebra family (𝔽_t) indexed by all t∈[0,+∞) with 𝔽_s⊆𝔽_t whenever s≤t.

Module theory: isomorphism class of an R-module M under invertible R-linear homomorphisms, the equivalence class of all R-modules isomorphic to M; this source restricts representatives to finitely generated R-modules.
Algebraic geometry: canonical structure sheaf O_Spec(R) of commutative rings on Spec(R), with O(D(f)) identified with R_f for distinguished opens and restrictions compatible with localization.
Commutative algebra: minimal prime of a commutative unital ring, a prime ideal minimal under set inclusion among all prime ideals, not simply a prime ideal of minimal positive height.
Set theory: reflexivity property of a binary relation R⊆S×S, namely (x,x)∈R for every x∈S.

Category theory: natural isomorphism between two covariant set-valued functors, a natural transformation with an inverse natural transformation; in particular its component bijections satisfy naturality in Y.
Probability theory: indexed family (A_i)_{i∈I} of measurable events A_i∈𝔽 in a common probability space.
Graded module theory: internal direct-sum decomposition M=⊕_{j∈ℤ}M_j into degree-indexed additive subgroups, so each element has finite homogeneous-component support.

Sheaf theory: stalk F_x of a sheaf F on a topological space X at x, the filtered colimit of sections F(U) over open neighborhoods U of x with restriction transition maps; for the structure sheaf O_X of a scheme the stalk is a local ring.
Category theory: an isomorphism H:E→E' of categories equipped with projections p,p' to C, satisfying p'∘H=p and having an inverse over C.
Field extension algebra: K-linear multiplication map m_α:L→L given by x↦αx; same typed construction used for field norm.
Real analysis/topology: open interval I⊆ℝ, possibly unbounded, such that for each x∈I there exists δ>0 with (x−δ,x+δ)⊆I; each point is interior to the real domain.

Field theory: rational function field k(X_i : i∈I), defined as the field of fractions of the polynomial algebra in an arbitrary set I of algebraically independent indeterminates over field k; polynomial elements have finite support.
query: field of rational functions in an arbitrary set of indeterminates over k

context: Category theory: fibre category E_U of a functor p:E→C over U∈C; objects are x∈E with p(x)=U and morphisms are arrows α:x→y in E whose image under p is id_U.
Algebraic geometry: for scheme morphism f:X→S, relative diagonal Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X uniquely satisfying pr₁∘Δ=id_X=pr₂∘Δ, formed from the universal property of the fibre product.
Algebra: identity e of a binary operation ⋆ on M such that e⋆x=x⋆e=x for every x in M.
Normed linear space: norm of difference vector v−a in V, equal to induced norm metric distance d(v,a).

Commutative algebra: formal derivative D:R[X]→R[X] of a univariate polynomial over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, uniquely specified by D(Σ_{i=0}^n a_i X^i)=Σ_{i=1}^n (i·a_i)X^{i−1}; a purely algebraic operation that works in positive characteristic without requiring analytic limits.
Category theory: zero object of a category, an object that is both initial and terminal, yielding distinguished zero morphisms in a preadditive setting.

Homological algebra: quasi-isomorphism between chain complexes, a chain map inducing isomorphisms in every homology degree; comparisons in the derived category can also be mediated by zigzags of quasi-isomorphisms.
Category theory: Grothendieck category ∫_C F of a strict contravariant category-valued functor F:C^op→Cat, with objects (U,x∈F(U)), base-compatible arrows and canonical projection to C.
query: Grothendieck construction of a category-valued functor

context: Category theory: ordinary comma category of functors F:A→C, G:B→C, whose objects are triples (a,b,u:F(a)→G(b)) and morphisms are compatible commuting squares. Includes (j↓H) and (H↓j) with their opposite arrow directions as different instances; no assumption u is invertible.
Measure-theoretic orthogonal polynomials: absolute moments ∫ |x|^k dμ(x) are finite for every prescribed nonnegative integer k.

Category theory: slice (over-)category C/U of a category C over an object U, with objects morphisms V→U and arrows commuting over U; a special ordinary comma-category construction but not the same concept as the general comma category or the existing iso-comma construction.
Discrete mathematics: integer label set {1,2,…,k} for a positive integer k, used as a finite k-element codomain with distinct labels.
query: finite set of k color labels

context: Measure theory: measurable function f:(X,Σ)→(Y,Τ) between measurable spaces, meaning f^{-1}[B]∈Σ for every B∈Τ; does not require probability on X, real-valued codomain or almost-everywhere equivalence.
Analysis: orthogonality of two polynomials relative to countably supported discrete positive weights, defined by a convergent weighted sum of their product equal to zero.
Commutative algebra: m-primary ideal I of a Noetherian local ring (R,m), with sqrt(I)=m and I primary; in this Noetherian local setting radical m is equivalent to m-primary.
Algebra: element r of an associative ring R (identity not required) is nilpotent if r^n=0 for some positive integer n. Do not restrict to commutative rings without justification.
Graph/set theory: unordered doubleton {u,v}⊆V for distinct vertices u≠v, serving as a possible loopless undirected edge.

Ring theory: associative ring R with a specified two-sided multiplicative identity 1_R, together with its additive abelian group and distributive multiplication; a unital ring is not merely a unital ring homomorphism.

Algebraic geometry: isomorphism of S-schemes X and Y for a fixed base scheme S, consisting of mutually inverse scheme morphisms commuting with their structure morphisms to S; in this source S=Spec(R).

Ring theory: element e in an associative ring, not necessarily commutative or unital, satisfying e·e=e; the Boolean-ring definition requires every element to have this property. Distinguish the property of e from the universal Boolean condition.

General topology: pullback X×_Y Z={(x,z)∈X×Z:f(x)=g(z)} equipped with the subspace topology induced by the product topology on X×Z, with canonical continuous projection maps. This realizes the categorical pullback in Top.
query: topological fibre product with subspace topology

context: Arithmetic: the usual total order on rational numbers as ordered fractions, enabling comparison q>0, independent of the strict-positive-subset being defined.
Category theory: cocone from a diagram F:I→C to vertex Q, a compatible natural transformation F⇒constant_Q with arrows F(i)→Q satisfying diagram commutativity.
query: cocone morphisms F(i)→Q compatible with the diagram

context: Set theory: countable union ⋃_{n≥1}A_n={x:there exists positive integer n with x∈A_n} of an indexed sequence of subsets of X.

Set theory: equivalence relation generated by prescribed ordered pairs P⊆S×S, the smallest reflexive symmetric transitive relation containing P; here S is the disjoint union of F(i) and P identifies each x with F(u)(x).
Real analysis: convergence domain D={z∈ℝ:∑_{n≥0}c_nz^n converges} of a real power series with coefficients c_n, here c_n=a_n/n!.
Order theory and topology: finite chain Z₀⊊Z₁⊊⋯⊊Z_n of distinct irreducible closed subsets of space X ordered by strict inclusion; chain length n counts inclusions, not the number n+1 of subsets.
query: strict finite chain of irreducible closed subsets

context: Set theory: intersection ⋂_{i∈F}U_i of finitely many subsets of ambient X, including the empty-index intersection X; topology requires this intersection to lie in τ.
Group theory: conjugate of subset N⊆G by g∈G, the subset {gng^{-1}:n∈N} obtained by conjugating every element.
Number theory: integer divisibility m|(a-b), meaning there is an integer k such that a-b=km, with m nonzero here.
query: integer divisibility of a-b by m

context: Finite-dimensional linear algebra: n-by-n square matrices over a field K, n≥1
query: Square matrix of finite order over a field

context: Commutative algebra: finite collection of polynomial equations/relations f_j in a polynomial R-algebra, generating the ideal of relations used to present an R-algebra.
Commutative algebra: inclusion of commutative rings R⊆S both with multiplicative unit, with inclusion preserving the common identity 1_R=1_S.
query: commutative unital ring and common identity

context: Abstract algebra: additive identity 0_B of abelian group B, the unique element with b+0_B=0_B+b=b for all b∈B.
Elementary arithmetic: n!=1·2·…·n for positive integer n, with 0!=1, a finite product in natural numbers.
Set theory: indexed disjoint union ⨆_{i∈I}X_i formed from tagged pairs (i,x) with x∈X_i, retaining which component each element belongs to even when the underlying X_i overlap.

Elementary set theory: singleton {x}, the set containing exactly the specified element x, viewed here as one connected component; its cardinality is one even when the ambient topological space is empty (then no such x exists).
Real construction from rational Cauchy sequences: eventual strict positivity with a common positive rational margin δ>0, meaning ∃N ∀n≥N a_n≥δ, stronger than eventual pointwise positivity.
Graph/combinatorics: finite vertex enumeration as a bijection {1,…,n}→V, choosing an indexing order on V.
Category theory: cocone over the span B→A,B→C, namely arrows A→P,C→P whose composites from B agree.
query: morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B

context: Module theory: zero (trivial) R-module with one element 0 and zero addition and scalar action; nonzero final quotient M/(f_1,…,f_r)M means that quotient is not this module. Distinguish the zero module from the zero submodule before taking a quotient.
Field theory: field automorphism of E, a bijective unital field homomorphism σ:E→E whose inverse is a field homomorphism; fixing a distinguished subfield F elementwise is a separate condition.

Graph theory on a loopless simple undirected graph: a circuit here is a nontrivial finite closed trail, namely a positive-length sequence of adjacent edges beginning and ending at the same vertex, traversing no undirected edge more than once. Unlike a simple cycle, other vertices may recur; distinguish graph circuits from matroid circuits and directed cycles.

Homological algebra: a two-term chain complex of modules concentrated in homological degrees 1 and 0, with differential d_1:C_1→C_0 and zero modules in the other degrees. The single differential automatically has no nontrivial consecutive-composite condition.
Real construction: set R_D of all Dedekind lower cuts of rational numbers, used as carrier for cut-based real number model.
query: set of all rational lower cuts R_D

context: Group theory: group generated by one element g with g^p=e and no smaller positive period, hence p elements; in this source it is the Galois automorphism group.
Homological algebra: chain complex in an additive category, a sequence of composable arrows whose adjacent composite is the zero morphism.

Algebraic geometry: canonical structure morphism of a scheme X to the terminal scheme Spec(ℤ), induced by the unique unital ring maps ℤ→Γ(U,O_X) on affine charts and compatible with restriction and gluing.
Commutative algebra: apply ring homomorphism φ:R→S coefficientwise to polynomial P∈R[T], evaluate φ(P) at g∈S, and test whether result is zero.
Real analysis: N-th finite partial sum of a real sequence, s_N=∑_{n=0}^{N}a_n, with an explicitly finite upper limit.
Sheaf theory: support of quotient sheaf O_X/I, set of points with nonzero stalk, determining associated closed subspace.
query: support Z of quotient sheaf O_X/I

context: Category theory: two-sided cancellation conditions of a calculus of fractions, permitting suitable equalized composites after composing with arrows in S.
General topology: intersection E∩V_i of a subset E⊆X with an open subspace V_i⊆X, considered with the induced topology on V_i.
Multigraph theory: edge multiplicity of unordered pair {u,v}, the nonnegative integer number of edge copies connecting u and v in E.
Algebra: two-sided inverse b of a under associative binary operation with identity e, satisfying a*b=e=b*a, for each a in a group.
query: two-sided inverse element b for each a

context: Module theory: the canonical R-linear injection of a summand M_i into ⊕_{j∈I} M_j, sending m∈M_i to the family with m in index i and zero elsewhere.
Homological algebra: ith cohomology H^i(C^•)=ker(d^i:C^i→C^{i+1})/im(d^{i−1}:C^{i−1}→C^i) for a cochain complex, with im contained in ker.
query: ith cohomology of a cochain complex

context: Additive category theory: finite biproduct or direct sum of objects, simultaneously product and coproduct with compatible injection and projection maps.
